acceptanceCriteria.text: `updateTaskLifecycleState` (or a new CAS-guarded variant used by `transitionTask`) requires the expected prior `lifecycle_state`/`task_version` in its `WHERE` clause and returns/throws a structured conflict when `changes === 0`, mirroring the existing `commitCleanup`/`markCleanupLease` pattern.
`transitionTask` propagates that conflict as a typed result (not a generic thrown error) so callers can distinguish "illegal transition" from "lost a race against a concurrent transition."

A new two-OS-process test (following `task.concurrency.test.ts`'s child-process pattern) proves that two concurrent legal transitions from the same prior state result in exactly one success and one structured conflict, never two silent successes.
Every durable adjacent `(from, to)` state pair recorded via this path remains a legal edge in the transition graph under concurrent load.

issue.title: fix: guard task lifecycle transitions with expected-state/version CAS
